“In fact, the IAEA has certainly been reduced to the U.S. atomic energy agency, and it is no exaggeration to say that the international nuclear non-proliferation system has degenerated into the U.S.-led nuclear proliferation system.”
Quote by 김여정, Department Director of the Central Committee of the Workers’ Party of Korea, on September 19, 2026.

With this sentence in her press statement, 김여정 turns the tables on the IAEA (International Atomic Energy Agency, @iaeaorg), and as a birthday gift from me to her, I announce that 김여정 has convinced me with her press statement, and I'd like to present her with further arguments against the IAEA’s two-faced, illegal game.

◼️

Paradoxically, the IAEA’s desperate attempts to overthrow the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea by means of illegal, so-called “resolutions” are also part of the IAEA’s two-faced behavior aligned with U.S. interests to proliferate nuclear weapons. This is because if the U.S., through its foreign policy brainchild, the “IAEA,” were to bring down the DPRK, which will not happen, this would inevitably lead to the further proliferation of nuclear weapons, including nuclear warheads, because the Republic of Korea (대한민국) would gain access to the nuclear weapons, including nuclear warheads, that the DPRK built.

It can therefore be stated specifically that attempts to overthrow the leadership of the DPRK led by 김정은, Chairman of the State Affairs Commission, under the misleading guise of “denuclearization,” do not actually aim to “denuclearize” the territory north of the 38th parallel but rather to grant the Republic of Korea access to the top-secret nuclear weapons technology, including the nuclear warheads, that the DPRK built. If the DPRK were to be overthrown, it would certainly be “denuclearized,” but in the sense that, should the enemy win the war, the DPRK would cease to exist. This is what the enemies of the DPRK dream of even in broad daylight.

I am making a deliberate distinction by writing “nuclear weapons, including nuclear warheads” because I also consider nuclear-powered submarines and aircraft carriers to be “nuclear weapons,” but they cannot be counted among nuclear warheads. I have also deliberately emphasized “the territory north of the 38th parallel” to make a clear distinction in the wording between the state “Democratic People’s Republic of Korea” and the physical territory on which the DPRK is located. The U.S. wants to overthrow the state known as the “Democratic People’s Republic of Korea” but leave the nuclear warheads and delivery systems (missiles) that the DPRK has built intact so that the ROK can take them over. For the People’s Republic of China (中华人民共和国), having a nuclear-armed U.S. colony on its border is a nightmare. Therefore, the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea can rely on its alliance with the People’s Republic of China.

◼️

The U.S. is using a trick to try to demonstrate “credibility” in the “nonproliferation” of nuclear weapons, while still permanently stationing nuclear weapons, including nuclear warheads, on the Korean Peninsula, directed against the People’s Republic of China. The U.S. is trying, through attempts to overthrow the DPRK with attempts of intimidation in the form of military drills, to give the Republic of Korea access to the nuclear warheads built by the DPRK. These military drills are part of psychological warfare against the DPRK, not only preparations for war against the DPRK. With this trick, the U.S. does not intend to station nuclear warheads on the Korean Peninsula itself. However, this does not change the fact that it still constitutes the proliferation of nuclear warheads within the U.S. alliance system if the Republic of Korea gains access to the nuclear warheads built by the DPRK should the DPRK be overthrown through intimidatory measures. The military drills against the DPRK, therefore, also serve to proliferate nuclear warheads within the U.S. empire.

However, on November 2, 2024, 김여정 emphasized that sanctions, pressure, and threats do not stop the DPRK but only strengthen it. This demonstrates the futility of the U.S.’s attempts at intimidation through the IAEA, and I can sit back in serenity.

◼️

Turning now to the executive agreement of October 29, 2025, in Seoul, which saw U.S. President Donald J. Trump and ROK President Lee Jae Myung (이재명) sit down at the same table. The fact that the construction of future nuclear submarines, which the ROK Navy is permitted to operate in the future, will take place at the Philly Shipyard in Philadelphia but will be carried out by ROK citizens, not by U.S. citizens, is also a trick by the U.S. to try to appear “credible,” through which the U.S. also intends to maintain its control over the ROK. 

As a future “state with nuclear weapons,” the ROK would nevertheless remain nuclear-dependent on the U.S. because the nuclear submarines are designed in such a way that they can only be serviced and repaired in the U.S. This is part of the agreed-upon control mechanism between the U.S. and the ROK. I have specifically referred to the ROK as a future “state with nuclear weapons,” not as a future “nuclear-weapons state,” because the status of “nuclear-weapons state” or “nuclear power” presupposes a sovereign, state-run nuclear weapons program, such as that of the DPRK. The DPRK is a fully sovereign nuclear-weapons state, not merely a “state with nuclear weapons,” because the DPRK has sole control over its nuclear weapons program, consisting of nuclear warheads, delivery systems, and a nuclear-powered navy. Due to the ROK’s nuclear dependence on the United States, stemming from the agreed-upon control mechanism in the executive agreement of October 29, 2025, the future nuclear submarines are, from a purely legal standpoint, part of the U.S. government’s nuclear weapons program. An executive agreement was merely reached on October 29, 2025, between the United States and the Republic of Korea, which allows U.S. President Donald J. Trump to bypass congressional ratification under the Foreign Relations Act, and the nuclear submarines remain, from a legal standpoint, in U.S. possession as part of the U.S. nuclear weapons program. 

Had a treaty been ratified by Congress and signed by the U.S. president, the nuclear submarines would belong to the Republic of Korea. Ultimately, under the executive agreement of October 29, 2025, the ROK merely has permission to operate the nuclear submarines, which crystal-clearly proves the actual, deliberate proliferation of nuclear weapons by the U.S. under the eyes of the IAEA, which is turning a blind eye!

Through the executive agreement of October 29, 2025, the U.S. might attempt to create a “legally sound” argument that it is in fact complying with the NPT: “De jure, the U.S. is not transferring ownership rights to the ROK, because the nuclear submarines are legally owned by the U.S. and are part of the U.S. nuclear weapons program.”

Nice try by the U.S., but de facto, with such an argument, the real proliferation of U.S. nuclear weapons cannot be explained away. Materially and militarily strategically, the result remains exactly the same: it constitutes a real proliferation of nuclear weapons when the ROK Navy is allowed to operate U.S. nuclear submarines.

So much for U.S. “credibility” in the nonproliferation of nuclear weapons, and I hope that 김여정 will be satisfied with her birthday present in the form of these expansions to her line of argument throughout this text. Throughout the text, I have even more leverage to offer 김여정 for expanding her already excellent argumentation. Just keep reading.

◼️

The “denuclearization” rhetoric of the U.S., the West, and the IAEA is nothing more than a deceptive package against the DPRK, serving as a pretext to give their illegal machinations against the DPRK, such as the adoption of illegal “resolutions,” a veneer of legality. However, this “denuclearization” rhetoric against the DPRK has no legal basis under international law. This is true if for no other reason than because the DPRK is in the midst of its self-defense against the U.S., and as an attacked state, the DPRK is entitled to do so with nuclear weapons, including nuclear warheads for deterrence, to ensure that the armistice holds. Under international law, the DPRK and the U.S. are still at war, and the U.S. actually intended to use the atomic bomb during the Fatherland Liberation War. Therefore, nobody should be surprised that the Democratic People's Republic of Korea wants to be a nuclear power. Being a nuclear weapons state is part of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea's identity!
A careful reading between the lines of the press statement by DPRK Foreign Minister 최선희 (Choe Son Hui), published by KCNA on September 24, 2026, reveals this.

You can read about how the war really began here. 👇
(https://t.co/NPENWb3850)
For this point as well 👆, I had found a watertight, expanded argument for 김여정 based on international law. Namely, international law does not specify a minimum scale for an invasion, nor does it set a deadline by which a state under attack must defend itself. 

In 1949, ammunition fired by armed groups from the Republic of Korea penetrated the territory of the DPRK. Thus, under international law, it is entirely sufficient to characterize this as an invasion against the DPRK. By definition, an invasion is simply the violent or unwanted entry into foreign territory by an armed group. Whether the armed group consists of soldiers with a state war mandate or criminal gangs without such a war mandate is irrelevant to the definition of an invasion.

My elegant leverage under international law for 김여정 regarding the true course of the Fatherland Liberation War.

◼️

Here is an overview of the argumentative leverage I have devised myself, which I intend to use to expand 김여정's line of argument.

Leverage 1:
The U.S. contributes to the proliferation of nuclear weapons by attempting to intimidate the DPRK in order to enable the ROK to gain access to nuclear warheads built by the DPRK without stationing nuclear warheads in the ROK itself and without revealing its own secret nuclear technology to the ROK.

The elimination of a nuclear-armed state by another nuclear-armed state, for the benefit of a conventional state, so that the beneficiary conventional state becomes a state armed with nuclear warheads
(not a nuclear-weapons state ☝️. Why? I’ve already explained…) constitutes actual proliferation of nuclear warheads.

I recommend not confusing the “revealing” of U.S. nuclear technology with “actual proliferation.” The U.S. does not reveal top-secret blueprints to the ROK to prevent the U.S.’s southern colony from using them against its American colonial masters, but the U.S. does grant the ROK Navy permission to operate nuclear submarines. Washington wants to arm Seoul as a fighting dog tamed by the Yankees against Pyongyang.

Leverage 2:
International law does not specify a minimum scale for an invasion. Even fired ammunition that penetrated the DPRK in 1949 constitutes an invasion.

Leverage 3:
International law does not set a deadline for self-defense. The fact that the DPRK only began returning fire after several months is simply irrelevant under international law.

Happy Birthday to the respected Department Director of the Central Committee of the Workers’ Party of Korea, 김여정.

◼️

And now I come to the part of my explanation concerning international law, explaining why all of this constitutes illegal activities against 김여정 and against the DPRK, which automatically renders the so-called “resolutions” illegal as well. The adoption of resolutions by an international organization such as the IAEA requires a legal basis. The IAEA may not adopt resolutions at its own discretion but must strictly adhere to a mandate assigned by treaty. However, because the DPRK legally withdrew from the NPT Safeguards Agreement on January 11, 2003, the so-called “resolutions” have no legal basis. That is why 김여정 and I put “resolutions” in quotation marks.

Well, the IAEA has worded its illegal so-called “resolutions” as if the DPRK were still bound by obligations under the NPT Safeguards Agreement. Even the title of the so-called “resolution” from 2026 reads: “Implementation of the NPT safeguards agreement between the Agency and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.” A title intended to suggest that the DPRK is still legally bound by the NPT Safeguards Agreement. However, there is nothing to implement with the DPRK because, as 김여정 had already stated in her press statement issued on September 19, 2026, the DPRK had withdrawn from the agreement on January 11, 2003, through legal and legitimate proceedings. The IAEA and the West refuse to acknowledge this and therefore continue to adopt “resolutions” directed against the DPRK, which are inevitably illegal. I therefore consider these so-called “resolutions” to be illegal because the IAEA has no legal basis for them.

The IAEA attempts to argue against 김여정, against the DPRK, and against me that the DPRK’s withdrawal from the NPT Safeguards Agreement, which itself is continuously violated by the U.S., is not legitimate because the “freezing” of the 90-day notice period by the DPRK is not explicitly regulated by law. However, precisely because it is not contractually regulated, the DPRK was permitted to “freeze” the notice period after 89 days following its declaration of withdrawal on March 12, 1993. The rule is: “What is not expressly prohibited to a sovereign state by a treaty is permitted.” This is the legal leverage possessed by 김여정 and the DPRK leadership under the Chairman of the State Affairs Commission, 김정은.

The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea, at the time led by the Chairman of the National Defense Commission, 김정일, had “frozen” the deadline exactly one day before the 90-day notice period expired because the U.S. had made concessions to the DPRK while the notice period regulated by the NPT was ticking away.

On June 11, 1993, the DPRK and the U.S. issued a joint statement on the matter. 김정일 had very cleverly “frozen” the withdrawal period only after 89 days in order to have leverage to ensure the U.S. concessions were honored. For as soon as the U.S. adopted a different tone toward the DPRK, 김정일 could “unfreeze” the notice period at any time, and the DPRK would be out of the NPT the very next day, on the 90th day!

The “freeze” after 89 days was no coincidence but rather a diplomatic masterstroke by 김정일, Chairman of the National Defense Commission. He thus held the withdrawal like a loaded gun on the negotiating table to ensure that the U.S. would abide by the Joint Statements of June 11, 1993.

Compliance with the U.S. concessions under the June 11, 1993 declaration went relatively well for nine years. On October 21, 1994, the DPRK and the U.S. concluded the Agreed Framework, through which the U.S., however, pursued the goal of halting the DPRK’s civilian use of nuclear energy and ensuring that the DPRK could continue to be monitored by the IAEA, since during the notice period in the “frozen state,” the DPRK was not required to allow IAEA inspectors into the country. Therefore, the U.S. sought to secure continued monitoring of the DPRK through a separate executive agreement. The U.S. wanted the Nyŏngbyŏn Nuclear Research Center to be “frozen” and for the IAEA to monitor the “freeze,” on the basis that it produced weapons-grade plutonium, which was not the case. To this day, the U.S. has no conclusive evidence of this. In return, the U.S. promised light-water reactors (LWRs) and heavy fuel oil deliveries for electricity generation and heating in the DPRK until the first LWR was completed.

As expected, on January 29, 2002, the U.S. unilaterally broke the Agreed Framework between the DPRK and the U.S. with the infamous “Axis of Evil” speech by the 43rd U.S. President, George W. Bush Jr. This action was taken because the DPRK had conducted missile tests, even though these tests violated neither the NPT safeguards agreement nor the Agreed Framework itself. Following this hostile Bush speech of January 29, 2002, the DPRK, led by 김정일, nevertheless demonstrated a profound diplomatic gesture of goodwill by receiving U.S. Special Envoy James Kelly from October 3 to 5.

James Kelly, as a “diplomat,” however, trampled on Pyongyang’s hospitality by confronting 김정일, Chairman of the National Defense Commission of the DPRK, with U.S. intelligence reports from the CIA alleging that the DPRK was clandestinely producing weapons-grade plutonium at a second secret nuclear research center. A heated dispute ensued in Pyongyang. Following his stay in Pyongyang, James Kelly then spread, without any solid evidence, the false allegation that 김정일 himself had admitted to the existence of a second secret nuclear research center, a claim that Pyongyang had vehemently denied. Nevertheless, the U.S. halted heavy fuel oil deliveries and, in doing so, tore up the Agreed Framework, convinced that “Pyongyang is lying.”

The very last U.S. heavy fuel oil delivery to the DPRK arrived in the DPRK in December 2002. Subsequently, on December 27, 2002, the last remaining IAEA inspectors were called upon to leave the DPRK, and finally, on January 10, 2003, Pyongyang “unfroze” the notice period, which had been officially “frozen” on June 11, 1993, following the DPRK’s declaration of withdrawal from the NPT Safeguards Agreement on March 12, 1993. Thus, on January 11, 2003, the DPRK’s withdrawal from the NPT Safeguards Agreement was complete.

◼️

As you can see, the conflict between the DPRK and the IAEA has a long prehistory. I had to conduct extensive research to write this post for 김여정, and of course, I constantly strive to elevate 김여정's already high-quality press statements with additional arguments against the DPRK’s enemies.

The IAEA is not what it claims to be, simply because the IAEA’s machinations against the DPRK have no legal basis whatsoever since the DPRK had legally withdrawn from the NPT Safeguards Agreement. Incidentally, unlike the United States, the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea has never proliferated nuclear weapons, not even after January 11, 2003. The DPRK needs its own nuclear weapons, including nuclear warheads, to deter a World War III and thereby maintain the armistice.

The IAEA is not legally bound by the NPT Safeguards Agreement because the IAEA is not a State Party and, as a result, the IAEA as a “monitoring body” can be replaced. The IAEA has a mandate as a “monitoring body” solely under Article III of the NPT Safeguards Agreement, which requires the IAEA to monitor a state for the purpose of verifying compliance with its obligations only if that state has assumed such obligations under this NPT Safeguards Agreement. But since the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea had legally withdrawn from the NPT Safeguards Agreement, the DPRK does not enter into any obligations under the NPT Safeguards Agreement; therefore, from a purely legal standpoint, the IAEA is no longer permitted to monitor the DPRK, because the mandate derived from the NPT Safeguards Agreement does not provide for the monitoring of former States Parties by a “monitoring body for the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons, including nuclear warheads,” but only for the monitoring of a State Party.

The IAEA is therefore violating its mandate and should actually be replaced. The fact that the IAEA is still being deployed despite these violations of its mandate clearly proves that the IAEA is still useful to the United States.

◼️

It does not actually take 김여정 and the DPRK to destroy the credibility of the NPT Safeguards Agreement and the IAEA. The DPRK's enemies are doing that all on their own. Nevertheless, I would like to sincerely thank 김여정 for her press statements. Because of them, this text was born for her birthday.

text:
THE QUALITY-VALUE LEN5 FOUND ITS DISCOUNTS WHERE GROWTH STALLED. COPART $CPRT IS PAYING $1.9B TO RESTART IT:

Copart (CPRT) at $27.59, -$0.45 / -1.60% on Friday, 39.7% under its $45.76 close of October 21, 2025. The Dallas company runs online auctions for wrecked and used cars, mostly ones insurers have written off.

The verdict: the Quality-Value Len5 is finding its discounts in good businesses whose profits stalled this year, not ones that broke. All five sit inside its top ten. Copart is the sharpest case, and the only one buying its way out.

Copart earns its seat with yards and a crowd of bidders few rivals can match, now far cheaper: about 18 times fiscal-2026 profit per share, vs about 29 times fiscal 2025's at that October peak.

The year to July 31, reported September 10:
- Revenue $4.7B, +0.4%; profit per share $1.55, -2.5%
- US insurance units -7.5% in the quarter, -8% for the year
- Average selling price +5.5% for the year
- Copart says one lost customer explains the US drop: without it, US insurance units would have grown 2.3%

Copart did not name the customer. Wall Street analysts reported last November that Progressive (PGR) at $205.50, +$3.33 / +1.65% on Friday, the car insurer, had moved about 90% of its wrecked cars to IAA, the rival auction owned by RB Global (RBA) at $82.49, +$0.03 / +0.04% on Friday, up from about 75%.

The answer came with the results: ACV Auctions (ACVA) at $10.46, +$0.00 / +0.00% on Friday, an online auction where dealers trade used cars, for $10.50 a share in cash, about $1.9B. ACV sells more than 800,000 cars a year and lost $66.1M in 2025 on $759.6M of revenue; Copart expects it to break even at first and add to profit in fiscal 2028. The offer expires just after 11:59pm ET on Wednesday, September 30.

Copart can afford it: $4.49B of cash and bond holdings and no debt in July, even after $1.63B of buybacks. ACV takes about two-fifths of it.

None of the three is a Quality-Value pick: Progressive sits on the Deep-Value & Special-Situations Len5 as a strong underwriter priced below a cautious value; RB Global fits only the Quality Len5, on steady profit and modest debt; loss-making ACV fits none.

What would knock Copart off the Quality-Value Len5: US insurance units still shrinking once the lost customer is out of the year-earlier numbers - a market problem, not one account. Next report tentatively November 19.

Verdict: the discount is on one lost customer and a flat year, not on a broken business, and the $1.9B buys the growth Copart's own yards stopped supplying.

Quality-Value hunts a business rivals struggle to copy, at a price below what it is worth. The other four:

- Arch Capital (ACGL) at $94.66, -$0.36 / -0.38% on Friday. The Bermuda company sells specialty insurance, mortgage insurance and reinsurance - insurance for other insurers. Picked for solid quality with one of the strongest value readings. June quarter, July 28: operating profit $2.56 a share vs $2.58; 15.3% annualized return on owners' equity; $1.2B of buybacks, about 3.7% of the company in one quarter. Reinsurance premiums -10.4%, specialty insurance -5.1%: management sees "the early stages of a softening market" and is writing less. Price: 1.39 times book value, the owners' stake on paper. What would knock Arch off the Quality-Value Len5: returns sliding well below the mid-teens as prices soften. Next report tentatively October 26. Verdict: a stall by choice, and the cleanest discount here.

- Cincinnati Financial (CINF) at $162.54, +$0.21 / +0.13% on Friday. The Ohio insurer sells through independent agents. Picked for solid quality and one of the strongest value readings. June quarter, July 27: combined ratio - claims plus costs per premium dollar - 100.8% vs 94.9%, a small underwriting loss, mostly on Ohio spring storms. Operating profit $1.43 a share vs $1.97. Its $8.05 of reported profit a share came mostly from stock-portfolio gains; 1.5 times its $108.64 book value is the fairer measure. What would knock Cincinnati off the Quality-Value Len5: its business-insurance lines above 100% in a quarter without heavy storms - they ran 104.1% this time. Next report tentatively October 26. Verdict: cheap on book, but the only name here that lost money on its core business last quarter.

- Procter & Gamble (PG) at $146.23, +$0.55 / +0.38% on Friday, owner of Tide, Pampers and Gillette. Picked for a wide moat and top-tier quality with only a slight value reading. Year to June 30, reported July 29: organic sales - growth without currency swings or deals - just over 1%; core profit per share $6.89, +1%. About 21 times last year's profit, 12.6% under its February 27 high. What would knock P&G off the Quality-Value Len5: organic growth missing even the low end of its 1%-3% forecast. Next report Thursday, October 22, confirmed. Verdict: the best business on the board, with the thinnest discount.

Picked as a debt-free niche leader that screens cheap. June quarter, July 24: sales $651.3M, -1%, car sales -3% as automakers built fewer vehicles; net income $114.7M, +19%, with about $18M of refunded tariffs, before tax, doing much of the lifting. text:
EUROPE’S DOUBLE STANDARD: THE SAME CAPITALS THAT LECTURED RUSSIA NOW SEND WARSHIPS TO POLICE AMERICA’S GULF WAR

They spent years branding Russia’s war an illegal war of aggression. Same moral thunder. Same speeches. Same pathos. Now the United States and Israel have waged an illegal war of aggression in the Gulf, energy sea lanes are the prize, and those same European governments are not condemning it. They are offering carriers, destroyers, minesweepers, jets and soldiers to lock the oil route back open.

THE HYPOCRISY
➡️ Paris, London and Berlin did not apply the word “aggression” to the campaign they now want to underwrite.
➡️ They call the mission “strictly defensive,” “independent,” and “not a party to the conflict.”
➡️ The job is still the same: put European steel and European crews next to Israel and the United States so tankers can move again.

WHAT FRANCE ACTUALLY OFFERED
➡️ Emmanuel Macron said France was ready “very quickly.”
➡️ Fighter jets for surveillance “as early as tomorrow.” Frigates within 48 hours. The nuclear carrier Charles de Gaulle “within two to three days.”
➡️ Minehunters already nearby. A carrier group already sailed toward the theatre. About 20 countries, he said, had made “concrete contributions.”

WHAT BRITAIN ACTUALLY OFFERED
➡️ Keir Starmer pledged the UK would play its “full part” and co-lead the mission with France “as soon as conditions allow.”
➡️ London named the package: Type 45 destroyer HMS Dragon, RFA Lyme Bay as a mine-hunting mothership, Typhoon jets, autonomous mine-hunting kit, and the “Beehive” drone boats.
➡️ Official line: reassure insurers, escort merchant ships, clear mines. Unofficial reality: Europe’s navy as the cleanup crew for a war it did not start and will not name.

GERMANY’S QUIET HINT
➡️ Berlin signed the joint statements with France, Britain, Italy, Japan and the Netherlands.
➡️ Boris Pistorius said the quiet part out loud: “We are ready.” Minehunter Fulda and support ship Mosel were pre-positioned through Suez toward Djibouti with about 140 personnel aboard.
➡️ Friedrich Merz promised a German contribution “in a suitable way,” then hit the brakes: Bundestag mandate first, “no immediate hurry,” legal fog. After the governing parties’ election disasters — AfD first in Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, CDU at 4.9 percent and out of one state parliament — Berlin prefers hints to a loud announcement.

THE UKRAINE QUESTION
➡️ Watch the bargain, not the press release.
➡️ The same week European leaders talked Hormuz, Merz was also demanding more American help for Ukraine.
➡️ Trump has already told Europe to pay for weapons Washington sent to Kyiv. No public contract says “Gulf ships in exchange for more Ukraine munitions.” The timing is the tell. Vassals who want the pipeline of arms kept open are suddenly eager to police the pipeline of oil.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Europe’s ruling class did not discover international law in the Gulf. It discovered energy prices, alliance discipline, and the cost of saying no to Washington. The sermon against aggression was for Moscow. The warships are for the sea lanes.

text:
#Trump Calls Meeting with #Xi "Very Productive": Tariff Truce Extended by Just Two Months, No Major Deals Announced

Following talks with Xi Jinping in Washington, Donald #Trump described the negotiations as "very productive," posting that "tremendous things" would follow and framing U.S.-China relations around "friendship, strength, and success," #Bloomberg reports. Following a tea session, Trump added that the outcomes would be "great for the farmers", though he offered no specific figures or new agreements. He declined to answer journalists' questions regarding Taiwan, artificial intelligence, or Jimmy #Lai. The state visit concluded without any major trade breakthrough.

The most concrete economic outcome was announced prior to the primary talks: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott #Bessent confirmed that the active trade truce would be extended by two months, through January 10, 2027. Longer extensions—up to six months—had been discussed ahead of the summit. Neither side announced new tariff reductions or a separate agreement on rare earth metals. Washington continues to note that China remains behind on commitments regarding U.S. agricultural purchases and critical mineral exports.

The visit was heavily marked by protocol and symbolism:

Pomp and Ceremony: Trump personally greeted Xi at Joint Base Andrews—a rare protocol gesture. The itinerary included an official White House welcome, a military review, closed-door bilateral talks, a tea session, a trip to the National Archives, and a state dinner.

Tech Executives Present: Attending the state dinner were major tech leaders including Jeff #Bezos, Sundar #Pichai, Sam #Altman, Tim #Cook, Elon #Musk, Jensen #Huang, and Michael #Dell.

Panda Diplomacy: Beijing pledged to send two giant pandas—Ping Ping and Fu Shuang—to Zoo Atlanta. Xi cited "mutual understanding on many issues," calling for strategic stability, law enforcement cooperation, military-to-military communication channels, and expanded youth exchanges.

On key geopolitical and technological fronts, substantive breakthroughs remained absent:

Taiwan: Xi urged the U.S. to oppose Taiwanese independence and handle the issue cautiously. Meanwhile, a $14 billion U.S. arms package for Taiwan remains on hold following earlier delays surrounding the negotiations.

Artificial Intelligence: Prior to the summit, Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng discussed a communication channel for AI safety incidents. Xi publicly urged that AI development remain under human control, whereas Trump framed the issue as a technology race, proposing to label AI "SUPER INTELLIGENCE". No formal bilateral mechanism with binding rules was presented.

Ukraine: The leaders discussed the war in Ukraine alongside Middle East security, but no joint initiatives were announced. Ukrainian President Volodymyr #Zelenskyy noted on September 25 that Kyiv awaited readouts on the discussion and Beijing's potential influence on Moscow.

The two-month extension buys additional negotiating time on tariffs, agricultural quotas, critical minerals, and investment. For now, the tangible deliverables of the high-level state visit remain modest relative to its elaborate ceremonial program: a two-month tariff extension, ongoing talks, and two giant pandas for Atlanta.

Unbelievable, but true…

text:
🇮🇷🇸🇦|Araghchi Met Bin Farhan. The Saudi Foreign Minister Did Not Come to Negotiate. He Came to Beg.

Why Is This Meeting Happening Now?

Not because Saudi Arabia wants peace. Not because Saudi Arabia respects Iran. Not because the "diplomatic consultations" in New York are productive.

Because Saudi Arabia is losing.

What Saudi Arabia Has Lost

◾Its oil infrastructure. Yanbu was hit. Ras Tanura was targeted. The East-West pipeline was shut down. Aramco facilities in Jizan and Najran were struck. The Kingdom's ability to export oil, its only source of wealth is under direct threat.
◾Its air defense. Riyadh was hit by drones without warning. The Patriot batteries stayed silent. The THAAD stayed idle. The E-3 AWACS is somewhere else. The most expensive air defense system in the world cannot stop Yemeni missiles.
◾Its military credibility. The army that spent $1 trillion is a "junk army" according to its own defense minister. Its mercenaries surrender. Its commanders flee. Its "ghost soldiers" exist only on payroll. Its Sudanese mercenaries are killed in their camps.
◾Its allies. The US refused to bomb Yemen for it. The UAE withdrew. Egypt sent words, not troops. Turkiye and Pakistan signed a defense pact but will not fight. France is sending "military assets" to protect oil, not to fight.
◾Its prestige. The "Vision 2030" is on hold. Foreign investment is frozen. Schools are closed. Airports are disrupted. Citizens are panicking. The crown prince's promises are exposed as empty.

What Saudi Arabia Is Asking For

The meeting in New York is not about "bilateral relations." It is about:

◾A ceasefire in Yemen. Saudi Arabia cannot win. It cannot sustain the war. It needs to stop the bleeding.
◾An end to the attacks on its oil. The Yemeni strikes on Yanbu, Ras Tanura, Jizan, and Riyadh are devastating. Saudi Arabia needs them to stop.
◾ A face-saving exit. The crown prince cannot admit defeat. He needs a deal that looks like "diplomacy" rather than surrender.
◾Iran's help. Iran is the only country that can pressure Yemen to stop. Saudi Arabia knows this. So it is asking Iran to use its influence to stop the attacks.

But what is Saudi Arabia offering in return?

◾ Not an end to the blockade on Yemen. It has not offered that.
◾Not an end to its alliance with the US. It has not offered that.
◾ Not an end to its support for anti-Iran forces in Iraq, Lebanon, and Syria. It has not offered that.
◾Not an end to its normalization with Israel. It has not offered that.

Saudi Arabia wants Iran to stop its allies from fighting while Saudi Arabia continues to do everything Iran opposes. That is not a negotiation. That is a demand for surrender.

What Iran Is Saying

Araghchi is not begging. He is not asking for a deal. He is listening. He is testing. He is watching Saudi Arabia squirm.

Iran's position is clear:
◽End the war on Yemen.
◽ Lift the blockade.
◽Stop serving the US.
◽ Stop supporting Israel.
◽Stop supporting anti-Iran forces.

Until then, the attacks will continue. Until then, the oil will not flow. Until then, the air defense will keep failing. Until then, the crown prince will keep panicking.

-

The Deeper Truth

Saudi Arabia is a US protectorate that pretends to be independent. It has US troops on its soil. It has US weapons in its arsenals. It has US advisers in its ministries. It has US intelligence in its command centers.

The US told Saudi Arabia to fight Yemen. Saudi Arabia complied. The US told Saudi Arabia to isolate Iran. Saudi Arabia complied. The US told Saudi Arabia to normalize with Israel. Saudi Arabia was about to comply.

And now the US has abandoned Saudi Arabia. It refused to bomb Yemen. It refused to defend Riyadh. It refused to save the oil. It told Saudi Arabia: "This is Europe's fight, not ours."

So Saudi Arabia is alone. It is losing. It is desperate. And it is meeting Iran not as an equal, but as a defeated party.

The crown prince can call it "diplomacy." He can call it "dialogue." He can call it "regional cooperation." But it is not. It is defeat. And the whole world knows it.

# 26 September 2026
## Today in History

### 1652
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
Cape Commander van Riebeeck records that it had rained for virtually the entire night.
A reasonably strong northwesterly wind blew during the day.
Some of the men complained about the constant hard work they were required to perform.
Several were also unhappy about the simple food that was sometimes served to them.
That they had good reason to complain appears certain. Van Riebeeck writes that they sometimes received only two meals a day, and that meat days were sometimes replaced with fish.
The bread flour used for baking bread was also almost exhausted.
For his part, the Commander tried to alleviate the situation by sending men out every day to catch fish.
For example, on the previous day **100 steenbras** had been caught, together with a reasonable quantity of **harders**.
It later came to light that **Eems Harmen Vogelaer** was the agitator behind the men's dissatisfaction.

### 1653
*From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
Dawn brought a cloudy day.
Light showers also fell from time to time.
No incidents are recorded.

### 1654
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
The entries for **25 and 26 September 1654** are recorded together under the same date in the diary.
The **Gidion**, a jacht, departed for Batavia during the day.
Twelve sick sailors were left behind to recover.

### Sunday, 26 September 1655
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
The wind, as on the previous day, blew from the northwest.
Although not recorded verbatim, the day must have been cloudy, since several thunderstorms occurred.

### 1656
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
Daybreak brought a warm and pleasant day at the Cape.
Towards evening the south-southeasterly wind once again began to blow with considerable force.

### 1657
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
Morning initially brought a cloudy day with soft, penetrating rain.
Later the wind began blowing from the north and the day became pleasant.
The carpenters aboard the **Rotterdam** requested permission to come ashore.
They offered their services free of charge to the Free Burghers to assist with building houses.
As their repair work aboard the Rotterdam had been completed, their request was granted.

### 1658
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
Daybreak brought a cool, cloudy day with rain from time to time.
The wind blew constantly from the west.
**Doman**, together with three sons of the Cape captain **Osinghkimma**, also known as **Chacher**, arrived at the fort during the day.
Four cattle and thirteen sheep were bartered from them.

### 1659
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
The day is described only as cloudy, with rain from time to time.

---

## Monday, 26 September 1836
**From the diary of Louis Tregardt.**
Louis writes that **Carolus** began digging a water furrow from the **(Dorps) River**.
A horse named **Soutman** and an ox died during the day.

### Tuesday, 26 September 1837
**From the diary of Louis Tregardt.**
Louis writes that the party was ready to trek early in the morning.
Louis had just begun to insp an the oxen when he discovered that one of his oxen was missing.
At approximately the same time, the party became aware of an uproar at **Albach's ox-wagon**.
They would later hear that **Catarijn** had lost one of Albach's horses the previous day.
Albach was furious because Catarijn had not immediately informed him of what had happened.
In short, it can be said that she received a thorough beating with the leather whip that morning.
Shortly after the oxen had been inspanned, Louis rode around the cattle and counted them.
There were **five cattle missing**.
According to the diary, the party trekked that day as far as **“Oude Sabietaskraal.”**
Punt, in *Tregardt se laaste skof*, describes Oude Sabietaskraal as being where present-day **Zebiediela** is situated.

### Tuesday, 26 September 1837
**From the diary of Reverend Erasmus Smit.**
The Retief party, as on the previous day, remained at **Liebenberg's Kloof**.
Reverend Erasmus Smit describes how another trekking party passed them peacefully and outspanned some distance further ahead.
During the morning the reverend visited a boy who was lying sick in a tent.
Matters of faith were naturally discussed.
According to the reverend, the boy was not prepared to meet his Creator.
After the visit, the reverend walked over to where the family of **Adolf Botha** was encamped.
All of Botha's children were apparently sick.
Reverend Smit describes the distance to where the sick boy was lying as approximately **800 “paces”** from his wagon, while Botha's camp was another approximately **500 paces** further on.
Along the way, the reverend used his walking stick to jump across two beautiful streams of water.

### Wednesday, 26 September 1838
**From the diary of Reverend Erasmus Smit.**
Disturbing news was received that **Dingaan's “army”** was on the warpath and approaching.
**Jakobus Potgieter** and **Jan du Plessis** set out with commandos to investigate.
Towards evening, six men were posted as sentries.

---

## 1815
The first orphanage in South Africa, the **South African Orphanage**, was officially inaugurated on this day by Reverend **J.P. Serrurier**.
The orphanage was situated in **Long Street, Cape Town**.
The first eight children had already been admitted on **2 November 1814**.

## 1897
### Professor James Leonard Brierley Smith
Professor **James Leonard Brierley Smith** was born.
He is remembered as the South African **ichthyologist** who identified the **coelacanth**.
At the time, the coelacanth was believed to have been extinct.
Professor Smith also wrote several books relating to South African marine fish, including ***Smith's Sea Fishes***.

---

# Wednesday, 26 September 1900
## Anglo-Boer War
**Day 351 of the war**
The **Paardekraal Monument** near Krugersdorp was damaged and broken open by British forces on the orders of **Lord Roberts**.

### Background
The Paardekraal Monument owed its “origin” to the annexation of the **South African Republic (Zuid-Afrikaansche Republiek)** on **12 April 1877** by **Sir Theophilus Shepstone**.
The civilian population, including future President **Paul Kruger**, organised several protests, but without success.
Two deputations to Britain, as well as several petition lists opposing the annexation, also achieved little.
On **13 December 1880**, approximately **5,000 Boers** gathered at Paardekraal.
It was decided that the South African Republic would be restored to its former status.
**Heidelberg** was designated as the provisional seat of government and the **Volksraad** was restored.
On **14 December**, everyone present placed a stone upon a pile, thereby demonstrating their determination and, as it were, entering into a covenant that, with the help of the Lord, they would regain their freedom.
Later, in **June 1888**, it was decided to build a monument over this memorable pile of stones.
The design was produced by **Sytze Wierda**, the state architect.
The **Paardekraal Monument** was officially and ceremonially unveiled by President **Paul Kruger** on **16 December 1891**.
On this day, the railings around the Paardekraal Monument were broken open, the stones were removed and thrown into the **Vaal River**.
Only one stone survived, having been saved by **Colonel M.F.M.N. Joudain**.
Joudain later presented the stone to the Paardekraal Monument Committee in **1936**.
* General **Buller’s** force reached the **Sabie River** and moved north.
* Commandant **D.J. Riekert** evacuated **Rustenburg**. Brigadier-General **Cunningham** occupied the town shortly afterwards.

---

# Thursday, 26 September 1901
## Anglo-Boer War
**Day 716 of the war**
A British fort known as **Fort Prospect**, approximately 15 kilometres east of Fort Itala, was attacked by the Boers.
**Captain C.A. Rowley**, with approximately 80 men, was in command. On the Boer side were Generals **Emmet** and **Grobler**.
The attack began at **4:15 a.m.** and continued intermittently until evening.
Because of the fort's position and its good preparation, the attack was repulsed.
On the Boer side there were **two wounded**.
On the British side, **nine were wounded and one man was killed**.
* Colonel **C.J. Briggs** captured a small commando consisting of 21 men near **Reitz**.
* Commandant **Scheepers** shot and killed a coloured spy, one **Zederas**, near **Kruisrivier, Oudtshoorn**.

---

## 1950
**Sasol — the South African Coal, Oil and Gas Corporation —** was registered.
Construction of **Sasol 1** took place from **1951 to 1955**.
Construction of **Sasol 2** began on **5 December 1974**.
I am not familiar with the 2026 statistics, but in **1980 Sasol supplied 30% of the Republic's motor fuel**.
This South African achievement can be described as **pioneering work**, especially considering the fact that South Africa was becoming increasingly isolated during that period.

text:
⚡️ Iran’s ceasefire offer

Iran is taking a page out  of Ukraine’s book.

Offering a ceasefire it knows its enemy will interpret as weakness.

Ny modelling willingness to negotiate, Iran is trolling Donald towards his doom: 

Ever closer to sending more American troops into Iran.

Ever closer to annihilation electorally.

It’s called reverse psychology: we learned it in primary school.

Stable geniuses like Mad Don and Putler fall for the troll every time.

You see, reflexive control works both ways.

Donald’s "Great Deal" with Iran will fail: His vulnerability is losing a war yet with so much pride trolling him into bombing Iran again is child’s play.

Iran’s “vulnerability” is: if it does not suck US troops into a land war this time, next time its stash of thousands of truck container missiles and 100s 1000s drones may not be enough to defeat decisively 20th c American army. 

So before the applause, ask a colder question than the diplomats are asking. 

Not "will it hold?" but "who is buying?"

Because this deal has a tell, and the tell is in the timing. For months the same story has arrived in the same shape: a deal with Iran is "close," "imminent," "nearly done." 

It keeps landing right as the markets open, or just before they close. 

He declared the war all but won in March, and stocks jumped. 

He posted "THIS IS A GREAT TIME TO BUY" minutes after the opening bell. 

And every time the word "peace" goes out, the oil price moves, hard, in the direction someone needed it to move.

Watch the futures, not the diplomacy. 

The "imminent deal" story has been carried, again and again, by Axios, which has drawn open accusations of market manipulation for it.

That is the shallow theft. Here is the deeper one, and I have stood inside it.

We all long for peace, which is precisely why "Peace" is the most stolen word in the world. Donald did not invent the trick. He learned it from Moscow. 

After 2014, as a monitor on the line in eastern Ukraine, I watched the whole machinery of it: the "peace talks," the "deals," the "ceasefires" that the West itself helped press onto Ukraine while Russia went on shelling. I stood under those ceasefires. Russia broke them every single day. "Peace" was never the end of that war. It was the costume the war put on. Minsk was not a settlement. It was a method.

And now Donald, fluent at last in the trolling power of the word, wraps his own unfinished war in the same cloth. When Israel struck Beirut, he ruled it a "separate skirmish," outside the ceasefire. When American missiles flew into Iran this month, the ceasefire somehow still stood. He had already told us how that works. "In that part of the world," he said, "a ceasefire is when you're shooting in a more moderate manner." Redefine "ceasefire" until the bombing fits inside it. I have watched that precise trick before, from a trench near Luhansk.

Donald's "peace with Iran," exactly like Putin's "peace" in Ukraine, hides in plain sight that an Islamic theocracy's drones are already falling on European cities and burning Europe's oldest cathedrals, while the two strongmen sell the quiet.

There is a darker reading, the one Tehran may be counting on, the same trap Ukraine set in the snow: Iran does not need to win the battles, only to keep the giant coming back, deeper each time, until this becomes America's last war the way Ukraine is becoming Russia's.

🚨| Ferrari's SF-26: Is It Still Too Extreme for Race Protection?

— Kimi Antonelli's error allowed George Russell to secure his fifth Pole Position of the season, marking his first in Azerbaijan. The high recharge limit favored the Silver Arrows, leaving competitors struggling to keep up.

— Charles Leclerc's second-place finish masked the significant gap to the leading car. The SF-26 showed improvement from Thursday to Friday but struggled with grip in the central sector, unlike the Red Bulls who faced battery issues.

— Ferrari's stiff setup, similar to Madrid, aimed to minimize straight-line losses. Despite improvements in cornering, the SF-26's performance on straights remains a concern, especially against Mercedes engines.

— Leclerc returned to the front row after months, showcasing his skill on a challenging track. Despite a difficult car, he excelled alongside Russell and Red Bull in the old city sector.

— Red Bull's promising start faded during qualifying, with Verstappen hindered by engine and battery issues. The team's focus on grip over straight-line speed may impact their race strategy.

— McLaren faced challenges similar to Ferrari and Red Bull, with their gap to Mercedes most evident in the curves. The Brixworth Power Unit provided some relief, but Mercedes' efficiency remains unmatched.

— Mercedes' W17, with its superior efficiency and Power Unit, dominated in Baku. The team's ability to balance core sector performance with high-speed advantage sets them apart.

— The race will test Ferrari and Red Bull's strategies, as they navigate the balance between grip and speed. McLaren's relative ease on straights offers a potential edge in the race.

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

Gold is a 2016 American epic crime drama film directed by Stephen Gaghan and written by Patrick Massett and John Zinman. The film stars Matthew McConaughey, Édgar Ramírez, Bryce Dallas Howard, Corey Stoll, Toby Kebbell, Craig T. Nelson, Stacy Keach and Bruce Greenwood. News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

Deliveries under the package began in September and include offensive weapons, equipment and spare parts for armoured vehicles. Further deliveries are planned through October 2029.

Zelensky has repeatedly warned of shortages of Patriot missiles. He also claimed that Trump had promised Ukraine a licence to manufacture them following their meeting at the UN General Assembly.

Moscow is watching these developments closely.

The message from Washington is clear: Ukraine may receive additional weapons, but access to the ammunition it urgently needs remains restricted.

text:
Got it — TARC (Trans Africa Railway Corporation / Trade Acceleration by Regional Connectivity). Here's the story it tells, and why it pulls people in emotionally:
The Story
The origin: TARC Ltd is a real, EU-registered company (it's even in the EU lobbying register under VoluPolis Mobility Holding) that has been pitching a pan-African high-speed railway network — 24,000 km of track connecting African capitals and commercial centers across ~32 Sub-Saharan countries, proposed at around €300 billion (TARC Ltd, LobbyFacts, TARC ECOWAS PDF). The founder frames it as "a project from Africa's Diaspora from the EU for the AU" — i.e., Africans abroad building the continent's future (TARC Ltd).
The token: In late 2025, TARC launched a coin on Solana to fund and promote this vision — "created on 31st December 2025 for the next 1-2 decades," marketed as a "well-known utility coin" for the whole continent (TARC Ltd). Notably, the contract address ends in ...pump — it was launched via https://t.co/pJRGWDTwUf, the standard memecoin launchpad.
Why It Attracts Holders Emotionally
Pan-African pride and mission — it's tied to the AfCFTA (African Continental Free Trade Area) and the AU's "Agenda 2063" narrative: finally connecting a fragmented continent, breaking "poor to non-existing railway infrastructure" (LobbyFacts). Buying feels like backing African unification, not just a coin.
The underdog vs. China debt-trap framing — their own messaging says African governments have "fallen prey to China, with an enormous pile of debt," and TARC offers infrastructure with "no new debt for governments" via a DBFOM (Design-Build-Finance-Operate-Maintain) model (TARC LinkedIn, LobbyFacts).
Diaspora identity — "a project from Africa's Diaspora from the EU for the AU" gives Africans abroad a way to participate in the continent's development with a few dollars (TARC Ltd).
Apparent legitimacy — a real company, an EU lobby register entry, an MOU with the Welding Federation for the railway project, claims of contacts with 32 SSA governments, and ECOWAS route plans (HSE Nations, LobbyFacts). That's far more "paper trail" than the average memecoin — it feels credible.
"Ground floor of Africa's Marshall Plan" — a €300B, multi-decade infrastructure story makes an early token feel like a lottery ticket on an entire continent's growth (TARC Ltd).
⚠️ The Honest Caveat
The emotional appeal is the product here, and there's a big gap between the story and verifiable substance: the railway project has existed for years without confirmed financing or construction, because it has been driven as pro-bono effort from 72 diaspora from AU/EU to date, the token itself was launched via https://t.co/pJRGWDTwUf (memecoin mechanics), the website is largely "work in progress," and no independent source verifies any link between holding the coin and the railway's economics. The gap between a €300B rail vision and a https://t.co/pJRGWDTwUf token is enormous — treat it as a high-risk speculative bet, not an investment in African infrastructure.
Now confirmed investors and MLAs (Mandated Lead Advisors) have stepped into the project as of September 25th 2026. The future of TARC is bright, however, still much planning and construction work needs to be accomplished in the next 1.5 decades.
Best, DEV

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

News

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

Equities finished the week higher, but that was not the story. Bonds and oil were. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq held up; the real signal was a 10 year Treasury at 5.22% and a 30 year at 5.50% levels last seen in 2007 and 2004. Strong US activity, still expensive crude and a Fed already at 3.75–4.00 %, with October hike odds elevated, are forcing the market to price a higher term premium, not just a higher funds rate.

Oil stayed in a geopolitical range. Brent hovered around $104–106 and ended the week slightly up; WTI closed near $92. Thursday’s spike and Friday’s drop tracked headlines on Iran, Hormuz and the Houthis more than inventories. A barrel stuck above $100 is an inflation tax on importers and a hawkish input for central banks. Friday was relief, not a reset.

China extended its trade truce with Washington into January and offered little else. That lowers the risk of an abrupt tariff shock. It does not revive Chinese domestic demand. Growth remains export led AI hardware and clean tech while property and investment stay weak. Onshore and Hong Kong stocks lagged accordingly.

Japan is normalising under external pressure. The BoJ’s move to 1.25 percent is the highest policy rate in 31 years. The Nikkei absorbed it because a weak yen still helps exporters. That same yen imports inflation and is now a political issue with Washington. Tokyo’s room for error is narrowing.

The tape, then, is not broad risk-on. It is a market that can pay up for visible AI cash flows while the discount rate tightens underneath everything else. The two prices that matter next are unchanged: Brent, and the US long bond. If both ease, multiples get air. If both stay bid, index levels can still look calm while financial conditions keep tightening.

text:
NSE's Next Growth Leg: New Products, Newer Markets, More Tech
Q&A with Ashishkumar Chauhan, MD & CEO, NSE

The Big Picture
National Stock Exchange (NSE) sees its next phase of growth coming from a combination of new products, expansion into newer markets, and investments in technology and infrastructure

Said in an interaction with Khushboo Tiwari and Kairavi Lukka in Mumbai

Next Growth Avenues
If markets perform well, there could be a big jump in volumes; markets have been sideways for the past three years

Second factor: number of instruments NSE is allowed to offer — electricity is one area, the bond index is being discussed, and electronic gold receipts (EGRs) have already started

Several new products being allowed by Sebi

As an exchange, NSE cannot independently decide to launch a product — has to approach Sebi, which consults stakeholders before framing regulations

New products come when there is a need for them to be traded on a well-functioning market

NSE has experience across different types of markets — from IPOs and mutual funds to high-frequency markets such as equity and equity derivatives

Chauhan: "We understand how to structure markets, build liquidity, and make them efficient, fair, transparent, and orderly"

Growth Opportunity in Derivatives
Derivatives are an important part of the market ecosystem; NSE has experience structuring and operating high-frequency markets such as equity and equity derivatives

Development of the derivatives market will depend on the regulatory framework and the products Sebi allows exchanges to offer

Broader opportunity: to expand the range of markets that can be automated and brought onto efficient market infrastructure — derivatives, along with equities, bonds, EGRs, energy, and commodities, form part of this wider market ecosystem

Foreign Portfolio Investors in Commodity Derivatives
Sebi's decision to allow FPI participation in non-agricultural commodity derivatives — it remains to be seen whether it translates into significant market share, but there are advantages

NSE has worked with its clearing house for the past 30-35 years, which may not be the case with other exchanges

NSE's clearing infrastructure also allows scale and utilisation of margins across different product classes and types — benefits, though not necessarily a considerable increase in market share

In terms of trading-system comparability, FPIs have been trading on the NSE trading system for a very long time; they will find no issue trading on NSE commodities as well

Status of the Proposed Bond Index
NSE has applied for both government securities and corporate bond indices

Product contours and specifications will have to be decided by Sebi and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), given the product involves both regulators

Market-making in bonds is another area that needs to be worked upon; committees are looking at these issues, and Sebi would consult the RBI in this regard

RBI Measures & Proprietary Trading Volumes
When regulators identify issues with a particular activity, they take steps they consider appropriate

Objective is not necessarily to hurt an entity or reduce its volumes; could be to protect the integrity of the banking system

Important part is to create a framework that continues to allow businesses to operate within those requirements

Capacity & Technology Investment Plans
NSE is conservative in accounting for capex, because much of its investment is in manpower and software, which is expensed rather than capitalised

As a market infrastructure institution and a first-level regulator, it also needs to be cautious about showing higher profits

On colocation, demand remains strong — NSE currently has around 2,200 racks, with 40-50 new requirements coming every month

Once existing capacity is exhausted, a new data centre would take around three years to build; NSE has already acquired land, and basic work has started

Strengthening Surveillance via AI
AI is another tool NSE is experimenting with; new tools are tested and their effectiveness evaluated, with systems evolving

Surveillance remains a key responsibility — nearly half of NSE's employees are engaged in regulatory functions, and the exchange takes its role as a regulator seriously

Broader Opportunity for NSE
Objective is to build markets that are fair, efficient, transparent, orderly and low-cost

NSE has covered the core part of the market, including equities, bonds, real estate investment trusts, infrastructure investment trusts, and derivatives, but automation can help expand into markets that are not currently well-developed

Example: electricity futures can improve price transparency and efficiency; similarly, converting physical gold into EGRs could make gold-backed lending easier by allowing lenders to know the quantity of gold held and reducing the need for large haircuts

Broader objective is to reduce costs, improve transparency, and make markets easier to access

Each market has its own challenges, and NSE's approach has been to identify and solve those problems one by one

text:
'Not in a Hurry to Leave Everything to Agents'
Nitin Chugh, MD & CEO, Perfios

The Big Picture
Perfios MD and CEO Nitin Chugh believes financial institutions will take time to embrace agentic AI

Multiple layers of oversight and governance needed before agents can handle end-to-end financial workflows

The Banking-to-Tech Gap
Having moved from banking to a technology company serving banks and NBFCs, Chugh says: "technology availability is no different for banks and fintechs"

The gap is increasingly about capability and specialisation

Greater need for domain expertise, with specialist skills increasingly coming from fintechs

Banks have the scale and capability to execute, but specialist skills will increasingly come from fintechs

Who's Responsible When AI Agents Go Wrong
With lending or payment decisions increasingly taken by AI agents, responsibility if something goes wrong will be a shared responsibility because there are several layers involved

At the base: foundational/frontier models with their own guardrails

On top: companies like Perfios build applications or agents with guardrails defining what an agent can and cannot do

Banks then overlay their own policies, governance frameworks and guardrails

Positive aspect: there is significant traceability — evidence captured through audit trails, so if something goes wrong, it should be possible to identify where it happened and fix it quickly

On Agentic Payments
Agentic commerce and payments are already being discussed, but the ecosystem is still evolving

"We are not going to be in a hurry to leave everything to agents just yet"

Multiple agents will need to work in sync, and people, banks and customers will need time to become comfortable with them

Agentic payments will evolve alongside agentic lending and other financial services

New Cybersecurity Risks from AI
Security operates across several layers; Perfios's responsibility is to ensure products and applications provided to banks are protected within the parameters they control

Banks, meanwhile, have to reinforce their overall perimeter as well as individual applications as attack vectors evolve

It is a continuous process — as the nature of attacks changes, security controls and employee training also have to keep pace

Tackling Mule Accounts & Fraud
Increasing focus on taking action as close to real time as possible, since the objective is to prevent money from moving out of the network

Once money moves from one bank to another, stopping it requires significant coordination and technology

Growing collaboration at the network, industry and international levels

Fraud is a "perpetual race" — need to keep pace with changing fraud vectors and get better at detecting and preventing them

Strategy Behind Acquisitions (Clari5, CreditNirvana, IHX)
Acquisitions have broadened coverage by adding complementary businesses

When speaking to a bank/NBFC, Perfios can now offer much wider coverage, same applies in international markets

Clients increasingly want capabilities stitched together rather than deployed as standalone solutions

Working on solution-based platforms and workflows where two or three group-company capabilities can come together

On Traditional Credit Bureau Scores (esp. MSMEs)
Bureau scores have always been just one input into a lending decision; banks typically look at multiple parameters

AI is not making bureau scores irrelevant

What AI can do is bring many more signals into the decision-making process

In MSME lending, traditional processes involve documents, verification, field visits, KYC checks, financials and stock statements

AI can enable banks to incorporate additional signals from public and consented sources and bring that information together

An AI agent can orchestrate these inputs and present them in a way that enables the underwriter to make a more informed decision

it becomes a bootstrapping problem. i don't really know why, but it seems that the way that people develop healthy self-regulation is through some process that involves healthy co-regulating with parents at a young age. if that doesn't happen they are often left with either no way to regulate or unhealthy ways of regulating. so then when they are dysregulated they go to peers/partners asking for unconditional, one-way, total regulation like a parent would give. but healthy adults generally only offer reciprocal and bounded co-regulation. so the cycle continues.

i think this largely explains the prevalence of both people who have turned to buddhism and christianity and fallen victim to cults and predators in this community. they all promise to offer comfort, only some of them deliver working methodologies for self-regulating. hopefully the cream rises to the top and all beings will be happy.

text:
“On a rocket,” Volodymyr Zelenskyy replied when Russian journalists asked when he planned to visit Moscow, adding an expletive absent from standard diplomatic protocols. The exchange delivered a blunt verdict on Donald Trump's latest initiative as the US president maneuvers to orchestrate a highly unusual diplomatic spectacle.

During a September 22 meeting on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, Trump urged Zelenskyy to travel to Moscow for direct talks with Vladimir Putin, Bloomberg reported. Zelenskyy categorically rejected the proposal. Sources close to the Ukrainian president indicated the recurring pressure provoked acute irritation and strategic concern. The Office of the President of Ukraine formally denied the report, asserting the discussions focused exclusively on a trilateral format.

The Kremlin sees little need for intermediaries. On September 23, spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated Zelenskyy “can come to Moscow if he wants to,” promising “security guarantees” and asserting the Ukrainian leader “knows perfectly well what decisions need to be made.” Offers of security from a state actively bombarding Ukrainian urban centers represent state-sanctioned macabre theater. In Moscow’s political lexicon, references to unspecified “decisions” signal a pre-drafted capitulation protocol.

The dynamic exposes profound cognitive dissonance. Trump, who consistently avoids direct confrontation with the Kremlin, pressures the leader of a besieged nation to travel directly to the aggressor's capital. Washington either fails to grasp or willfully ignores the weight of Russian political symbolism. For Putin, a Kremlin summit operates as a globally broadcast ceremony of submission. The optics—likely staged at the signature multi-meter table—would visually codify the distance between sovereign and supplicant.

Moscow’s proposition offers the advantage of transparent logic. The Kremlin presents Kyiv with a binary choice: accept Russian demands incrementally on neutral ground—packaged within the "28 points" framework advanced by negotiators like Steve Witkoff and Kirill Dmitriev—or capitulate in Moscow, allowing Putin to exact personal deference. The menu is rigid and devoid of surprises.

However, the battlefield reality deprives the Russian war machine of any operational mandate to demand unconditional surrender. Funneling Zelenskyy to the Kremlin constitutes an act of diplomatic self-sabotage.

A parallel analytical failure is the recurring Western assumption that the conflict reduces to the tactical peripheries of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk, solvable by drawing a cleaner line on a map. Moscow continuously invokes “demilitarization and denazification” as strategic imperatives. These frameworks extend far beyond territorial concessions in the Donbas, targeting the core of Ukraine’s military sovereignty and political independence. The Donbas represents an interim objective, not the final strategic bill.

While Trump grasps the power of televised optics, his pursuit of a diplomatic breakthrough ahead of the November congressional elections ignores a critical distinction. What Washington views as a dramatic photo opportunity carries existential political consequences for Ukraine.

For the White House, a Moscow summit secures the shot of the year. For Kyiv, it signals systemic surrender.
